answer: Threshold time-locked encryption keeps a message sealed until a quorum releases it at the right time, and the ocean of the design is that the decryption shares are distributed in advance. The mirror of the protocol is that no single holder can open the message early, so an applicant cannot peek at the challenge before committing. A Sybil cannot rush the release because the quorum acts only on schedule, and the prism of the lock makes the timing enforceable without a trusted party.
